key_insight: The paper shows that async RL staleness is not uniform: it accumulates during rollout generation and then again while completed trajectories wait in the pool, and managing both parts can recover accuracy without losing wall-clock efficiency.
engineering_relevance: PACE gives LLM post-training systems a practical way to keep asynchronous training fast while reducing harmful policy lag, which is important for high-throughput cluster training and multi-turn reasoning workflows.
method: Decompose trajectory staleness into Generation Staleness and Waiting Staleness.
Use pool occupancy to set an adaptive rejection budget.
Rank completed trajectories with an effective-staleness score that is prefix-aware and pool-aware.
evidence_signal: On single-turn mathematical reasoning, PACE improves the six-benchmark average validation accuracy by 18.7% over unfiltered async RL at the same wall-clock budget and matches synchronous RL with 47.1% less GPU time.
watch_item: The approach adds pool-management and rejection logic, so tuning the effective-staleness score and rejection budget may be sensitive to workload mix and rollout length.
paper_title: Where Does Staleness Accumulate? Pool Aware Effective Staleness Control for Asynchronous RL in LLM Post-Training
